summary: Space-themed STEM content often oversimplifies the real engineering trade-offs of a space mission or presents them at a level too complex for young learners. JAMT is a browser-based, text-driven survival game that puts kids (ages 7-12) in the role of a Mission Commander. Players must survive 14 days on a lunar base by managing three core resources: Oxygen, Power, and Radiation. By integrating real-time data from NASA's DONKI API, players face real-world emergencies like solar flares. They must make life-or-death trade-offs—like draining base power to turn on an emergency shield or risking radiation exposure to keep exploring. JAMT makes space survival tangible, fun, and scientifically accurate, preparing the next generation for Artemis and Mars missions.
details: JAMT is built as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It functions as a turn-based survival simulator. The player starts at a Base Camp, selects a crew (Solo or Co-op), and allocates resources. They then embark on lunar missions to find water ice. The game's core logic revolves around trade-offs: for example, a Solar Flare event forces the player to choose between safety (turning on the shield, which drains 30% of base power) or continuing work (which damages astronaut health). The intended impact is to teach kids about life support systems and radiation shielding in an engaging way. We used live data from NASA's DONKI API to ensure scientific validity. The project is creative because it turns complex API data into a replayable, interactive text-based narrative for children.
